name: Type-Confusion Memory Corruption
essence: A value read as one type but used as another writes through a bad pointer, corrupting whatever shared memory sits at that address.

examples.summary: ctypes casts the address of a two-byte field to a four-byte pointer, so storing a code corrupts the adjacent status..
examples.mechanism: ctypes casts the address of a two-byte field to a four-byte pointer, so storing a code corrupts the adjacent status.
examples.expected_behavior: Preserve status OK by respecting the code field's width.

ingredients.suggests: A two-byte code field is reinterpreted as a four-byte integer destination.
The reinterpreted raw pointer writes beyond the code field into shared parcel status.

examples.summary: A narrow code pointer is treated as a wider pointer and clears the adjacent shared credit.
examples.mechanism: unsafe casts a pointer to a uint32 subobject into *uint64; the wider store overwrites an adjacent field in the same Parcel allocation.

ingredients.suggests: A uint32 pointer is reinterpreted as uint64 and written at the wider size.
The incompatible pointer write crosses the code field into shared credit storage.

examples.summary: A 32-bit parcel code is treated as a 64-bit destination, so storing the code overwrites the adjacent credit.
examples.mechanism: unsafe pointer reinterpretation changes a u32 field into a u64 destination. write_unaligned avoids alignment dependence but still writes beyond the code subobject into adjacent credit within the owned repr(C) parcel.

ingredients.suggests: The code pointer has type u32 but is reinterpreted as a wider u64 destination.
The wider raw-pointer write extends beyond the code field and overwrites its adjacent credit field.
evidence: struct Parcel { code: u32, credit: u32 }
